---
title: "Lab 03 — Statistical inference in R"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
survey <- read.csv("data/survey.csv")
sleep  <- read.csv("data/sleep.csv")
tooth  <- read.csv("data/ToothGrowth.csv")
h <- na.omit(survey$Height)
set.seed(2027)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab03", title = "Statistical inference in R", open = c("q10"))
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1  = "The 95% confidence interval for the mean height of the students is about...",
  q2  = "The one-sample t test of H0: mean height = 170 gives p = 0.0006. At the 5% level...",
  q3  = "In the Welch two-sample t test of height by sex, the estimated difference between men and women is about 13.1 cm and p < 0.001. The best interpretation is...",
  q4  = "var.test for the height by sex gives p = 0.002. Which statement is best?",
  q5  = "In the sleep data, the paired t test of the difference between the two drugs gives...",
  q6  = "The unpaired Welch test on the same data gives p = 0.079. Why does the paired analysis detect the difference?",
  q7  = "47 of the 236 students who answered smoke (anything other than Never). The 95% confidence interval for the proportion of smokers is about...",
  q8  = "A die is rolled 120 times and the counts of faces 1 to 6 are 14, 22, 17, 25, 16, 26. The chi-square goodness-of-fit test of a fair die gives...",
  q9  = "The chi-square test of independence between smoking and exercise (Smoke by Exer) gives p = 0.48 and R warns about small expected counts. The right reading is...",
  q10 = "In 1000 simulated samples, 95% t intervals for a mean covered the true mean in about 95% of the samples. Explain in your own words what '95% confidence' means, and say when the coverage can fall below 95% (give one situation from the lab)."
)
```

## What you will do

Check the numbers from the lab, then answer the questions. `survey`, `sleep` and `tooth` are loaded, and `h` holds the heights (cm) of the students with a recorded height. Finish by downloading the `.txt` file.

## Means

```{r t-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
t.test(h)$conf.int
t.test(h, mu = 170)
t.test(Height ~ Sex, data = survey)
var.test(Height ~ Sex, data = survey)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("(171.0, 173.7) cm", correct = TRUE),
  answer("(165.7, 178.8) cm"),
  answer("(160.0, 185.0) cm"),
  answer("(172.0, 172.8) cm"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("we reject H0: the data suggest a mean above 170 cm", correct = TRUE),
  answer("we do not reject H0"),
  answer("we accept H0 with probability 0.9994"),
  answer("the test is invalid because p is smaller than 0.05"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("Men are taller on average by about 13 cm in this sample; if H0 were true, a difference this large would be very unlikely.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("13.1% of men are taller than women."),
  answer("The p-value is the probability that H0 is true."),
  answer("Women and men have the same mean height."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  answer("the data suggest the variances differ, but Welch is the default regardless of any preliminary F test, so we do not choose the t test by this p-value", correct = TRUE),
  answer("the means are different"),
  answer("the variances are equal"),
  answer("the t test cannot be used at all"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Paired data and proportions

```{r pair-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=10}
x1 <- sleep$extra[sleep$group == 1]
x2 <- sleep$extra[sleep$group == 2]
t.test(x2, x1, paired = TRUE)
t.test(x2, x1)$p.value
smoke <- na.omit(survey$Smoke)
x <- sum(smoke != "Never"); n <- length(smoke)
c(x, n, x / n)
prop.test(x, n)$conf.int
```

```{r q5}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q5"]],
  answer("t = 4.06, df = 9, p = 0.0028: drug 2 gives about 1.6 more hours of sleep", correct = TRUE),
  answer("t = -1.86, df = 17.8, p = 0.079: no evidence of a difference"),
  answer("t = 4.06, df = 19, p = 0.0028"),
  answer("the test cannot be done because the groups are not independent"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q6}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q6"]],
  answer("The same patients took both drugs, and pairing removes the variability between patients.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The paired test uses a larger sample."),
  answer("The paired test assumes the variances are equal."),
  answer("The paired test is always more significant."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q7}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q7"]],
  answer("(0.151, 0.257)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("(0.047, 0.236)"),
  answer("(0.199, 0.236)"),
  answer("(0.05, 0.50)"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Chi-square tests and coverage

```{r chi-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=10}
obs <- c(14, 22, 17, 25, 16, 26)
chisq.test(obs, p = rep(1/6, 6))
chisq.test(table(survey$Smoke, survey$Exer))
n <- length(h)
sqrt((n - 1) * var(h) / qchisq(c(0.975, 0.025), n - 1))
```

```{r q8}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q8"]],
  answer("X-squared = 6.3, df = 5, p = 0.28: no evidence that the die is unfair", correct = TRUE),
  answer("X-squared = 6.3, df = 6, p = 0.39"),
  answer("X-squared = 63, df = 5, p < 0.001"),
  answer("p = 0.28, so the die is fair with probability 0.72"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q9}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q9"]],
  answer("no evidence of an association, though the approximation is doubtful; merge categories or use a simulated p-value", correct = TRUE),
  answer("strong evidence of an association"),
  answer("the test is wrong and gives no result"),
  answer("the variables are proven to be independent"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q10}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q10"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Interpret the 95% as a long-run frequency...",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
